name: Player-Conditional Replicated Stochastic-Measure Gradient
lineage_evidence: SAMPLING_VARIANCE_ATLAS:DT latent/time/bridge variance dominated 7/7 active rows
SAMPLING_VARIANCE_ATLAS:HJ independent-batch and latent/time/bridge variance dominated 22/22 rows each
INC-20260830-RSMG-PLAYER-STATE:the first implementation reused a pre-D replica bundle after D/E changed and was frozen as engineering-invalid

compared_implementations: invalid G1-02 RSMG shared pre-D bundle
prior_equivalence_audit.material_difference: PC-RSMG does not reuse the opponent-update replica bundle for G/F. It commits D and E, discards that bundle, and only then draws a fresh conditionally iid G/F bundle. This changes cross-player stochastic coupling while preserving each player's expected native UNSB gradient field at the state where that player is optimized. It does not average endpoints, change the time/domain measure, concatenate PatchNCE replicas, add a loss, or access paired targets.

unsb_object: the player-conditional stochastic gradient estimator of the sequential native D, E, then joint G/F UNSB game
formula: Let S_k and b_k be the current full state and one official batch-1 unpaired draw. Draw xi_DE^1,xi_DE^2 iid from the native stochastic measure and commit D with their mean gradient. Because L_E does not read theta_D, use the same iid pair to commit E. Let S_k^{DE} be the resulting opponent-updated state. Then independently draw xi_GF^1,xi_GF^2 from the native measure at S_k^{DE} and commit joint G/F with gbar_GF=(g_GF(S_k^{DE},b_k,xi_GF^1)+g_GF(S_k^{DE},b_k,xi_GF^2))/2. Adam is applied once per native player after averaging. The two bundles use four serial batch-1 forwards and are never concatenated.
identity_or_unbiased_condition: For p in {D,E}, conditional on the pre-opponent state and official batch, the two DE draws are iid and E[gbar_p]=E[g_p]. Conditional on the realized updated opponent state S_k^{DE}, the fresh GF draws are independent of the DE estimator, hence E[gbar_GF|S_k^{DE},b_k]=E[g_GF|S_k^{DE},b_k] and Var(gbar_GF|S_k^{DE},b_k)=Var(g_GF|S_k^{DE},b_k)/2. Setting pcrsmg_replicates=1 dispatches the original optimize_parameters path exactly.
target_inaccessibility_proof: Both player bundles receive the same official unpaired batch-1 tensors and draw only native latent, bridge-noise, time and PatchNCE randomness. Bundle count and order are fixed. No held-out pair, metric, domain-label controller or confirmation sample is addressable.

expected_applicable_state.condition: latent/time/bridge or independent-batch randomness dominates the observed update variation
expected_applicable_state.self_null_state: one replica is byte-identical to plain; at two replicas the expected per-player vector field and native stationary conditions are unchanged
expected_applicable_state.compute_only_risk: any gain is compute-sensitive because the method performs four stochastic forward/loss views per optimizer update

falsifying_experiment: Kill as engineering-invalid if the actual event order is not DE_BUNDLE,D_COMMIT,E_COMMIT,GF_BUNDLE,GF_COMMIT, if GF bundle counters do not restore exactly, if a coupled-game fixed-state gate finds conditional mean bias, if one-replica identity or resume is not exact, or if replicas create cross-image PatchNCE negatives. A valid negative e200 result closes only this two-replica player-conditional estimator.
compute_cost: approximately four native stochastic forward views per optimizer update: two shared by D/E and two freshly drawn for G/F; native player optimizer-step count and data exposure remain unchanged
memory_cost: replica graphs are executed/accumulated serially and the DE bundle is deleted before GF construction, keeping peak activation memory near a two-replica implementation rather than four simultaneous graphs
recovery_state_cost: replica count, update index, DE/GF bundle counters, bundle serial, last event schedule and ordinary Python/NumPy/CPU/CUDA RNG state

ablation_definitions.proposal_only: Apply the fresh two-replica player-conditional bundle only to G/F while D and E retain one native view.
ablation_definitions.observable_only: Draw and log the second DE/GF views but commit the first-view native gradients only.
ablation_definitions.projected_or_full: Use two iid replicas for D/E and, after their commits, a new two-replica bundle for joint G/F; no projection, auxiliary loss or endpoint averaging.

finite_step_coupling_change: PC-RSMG intentionally replaces native same-view cross-player correlation with player-conditional independent randomness. It preserves each player's expected loss gradient field at its realized optimization state, not the exact finite-learning-rate stochastic transition of plain UNSB.
unbiased_proof: Condition on the official batch and the state at which each player is optimized. D and E each receive the average of two iid native-measure gradients, so linearity gives the native expected field and independence halves variance. After their optimizer steps, the G/F bundle is redrawn independently; conditional on the realized updated D/E state, the same argument gives the native G/F expected field and half variance. This removes the conditional bias caused by reusing randomness that helped create the opponent state. Adam is applied once after each mean estimator. The finite-step cross-player noise coupling changes, but the expected per-player objectives and their stationary conditions do not.
